'''''Euphorbia ceratocarpa''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the spurge [[family (botany)|family]] Euphorbiaceae, native to the Island of [[Sicily]] and southern [[Italy]]. Growing to {{convert|1.7 |m|ft|abbr=on}} tall and wide, it is an [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] or [[subshrub]] bearing long, narrow leaves with a prominent white midrib,<ref name = SHOOT>{{cite web 
| url=  https://www.shootgardening.co.uk/plant/euphorbia-ceratocarpa
| title = Euphorbia ceratocarpa | publisher = Shoot Gardening | access-date = 25 February 2018}}</ref>
and clusters of green and yellow flowers in summer. The flowering period may be extended in favourable locations. It is valued in cultivation for its vivid flowers, and its ability to survive drought conditions. Though hardy down to {{convert|-10 |C|F|abbr=on}} it is seen at its best in a warm, sheltered position. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/31411/i-Euphorbia-ceratocarpa-i/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Euphorbia ceratocarpa'' | access-date=25 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 
| page = 38 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 February 2018}}</ref>

Like other members of the genus ''Euphorbia'', all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested. When cut it produces a milky sap which may cause intense irritation to hands and eyes.<ref name = SHOOT/>
